defects_found.description: The added closing-edge citation quotes הוֳא with a munah accent on the pronoun; Judg_oshb.txt carries no accent on that word (the mark falls on the following בָ֣א instead). Full-corpus verification against Judg_oshb.txt for all 173 frozen rows found this among 4 such cases; the deterministic citation sweep is explicitly disclosed elsewhere in this campaign (M8-Judg-061) as consonant-level only and not built to catch cantillation placement, so this falls in that acknowledged gap rather than contradicting the sweep's own claim. Does not affect the boundary argument, which rests on the fronted-pronoun-plus-qatal word order, not the accent.

The opening-verse citation for the true head of the span drops the meteg after the initial vav and misplaces the pashta accent by one letter relative to Judg_oshb.txt's וַ־יְהִי֩. Same class of defect as M8-Judg-119; consonants and word order are correct, only secondary diacritic placement is off.

The second אֲשֶֶׁר in the citation is given a munah accent; Judg_oshb.txt carries qadma at that position. Does not affect the pronoun-fronted-frame argument, which the decision correctly bases on the consonantal text and the presence versus absence of a new agent.

The rationale states the boundary is 'reinforced by the shared closing tag כָּל זֶ֣ה at both v16 and v17' and cites both verses with the same (tipeha) accent. Direct check against Judg_oshb.txt shows the two occurrences of כָּל זֶה actually carry different Masoretic accents - revia at 20:16, tipeha at 20:17 - so the citation for v16 is inaccurate and the 'shared tag' framing overstates the parallel as byte-identical when only the consonantal wording (kol zeh) actually recurs. The underlying structural point (a register-pairing tag between the two troop counts) still holds at the consonantal level and does not require reversing the boundary or the medium confidence rating, but the citation should be corrected and the claim narrowed to consonantal recurrence.

author_responses.json is not uniform: 76 round-1 (OL/LF) challenge responses live under each decision's 'challenge_responses' array, while 25 revision-round (RV/LFR) and the 3 special-verdict (frontier_defer x2, insufficient_evidence x1) responses are duplicated or side-keyed under 'challenge_dispositions' and 'peer_finding_responses', and the 5 sweep responses (SWEEP-*) live only in 'peer_finding_responses'. All 106 expected challenge ids (76 digest + 25 revision + 5 sweep) do resolve to exactly one boss ruling and at least one author response once these side keys are included, and every duplicate pairing checked (35 ids appear in both challenge_responses and challenge_dispositions) carries a consistent disposition with no contradiction. Not a defect, but the mixed schema is worth flagging for any future automated consumer of this file that only reads 'challenge_responses'.
